newsitem.title: CHINA: China aluminium firms face rising power prices.
newsitem.headline: China aluminium firms face rising power prices.

text.p: China's aluminium industry is faced by rising electricity prices that have pushed up costs and created mounting losses, the Economic Information Daily said on Tuesday.

"Constantly rising electricity prices have exceeded capacity of nonferrous firms, threatening the existence of the aluminium industry," it quoted a senior official of the China National Nonferrous Metals Industry Corp as saying.

In the first 10 months of 1996, total losses of China's 12 main aluminium firms hit 143 million yuan ($17.2 million), which compared with total profits of 1.548 billion yuan in the year-ago period, he said.
Output of the 12 main aluminium plants accounted for about half of the national total, the official was quoted as saying. He did not identify the firms.
Average electricity costs to the aluminium sector rose by 0.05 yuan per kilowatt-hour to 0.31 yuan in 1996, he said.
Power costs account for 38.1 percent of production costs in Chinese firms, or about 18 percentage points higher than the international level, he said.
The government should suspend collection from aluminium firms of special fees for construction of the Three Gorges dam and scrap additional charges, he said.
The government should also tighten its grip on electricity price rises and allow prices to fluctuate in line with aluminium prices, the official said.
